questions.question_text: Convert the following EER model into the relational model. Indicate the primary keys and the foreign keys of the resulted relations clearly.

criteria.point: Correctly identifies all entities from the EER diagram and creates corresponding relations
Correctly handles the superclass/subclass relationship (Instructor, Researcher) with appropriate mapping strategy (single relation, multiple relations, or shared PK)
Correctly maps all attributes including multi-valued and derived attributes
Correctly identifies and names all primary keys
Correctly identifies and names all foreign keys with proper references
Handles cardinality constraints (N:M, 1:N relationships) correctly in the relational schema

questions.model_answer: Person(SSN, Name, Address), Instructor(SSN, Rank, Salary), Researcher(SSN, GrantAmount, Publications). SSN is PK for all; Instructor.SSN and Researcher.SSN are FKs referencing Person.SSN.

questions.question_text:
Consider a relation R(A,B,C,D,E), with the following set of functional dependencies over R: F={A→BC, BC→E, E→DA}.
a) Find all the keys that follow from the given FDs using Armstrong's axioms, showing how you found them. (9 marks)
b) Is R in 3NF? Give reasons for your conclusion. (3 marks)
c) Is R in BCNF? Give reasons for your conclusion. If R is not in BCNF, convert it to a set of BCNF relations. (3 marks)

criteria.point: Correctly computes attribute closures to find candidate keys
Identifies all candidate keys (A, BC, BE)
Shows step-by-step application of Armstrong's axioms
Correctly determines 3NF status with justification
Correctly determines BCNF status and decomposes if needed

questions.model_answer: Keys: A, BC, BE. R is in 3NF but not in BCNF because E→DA where E is not a superkey. BCNF decomposition: R1(A,B,C), R2(B,C,E), R3(E,D,A).

questions.question_text:
Consider the database of a department store that includes the following tables:
ITEM(itemNo, itemName, dept, price, availableQty, cost)
EMP(eNo, eName, salary, comm, dept)
DEPT(dNo, dName, mgrEno)
SALES(idNo, eNo, soldTime, soldQty, soldPrice)
Write relational algebra statements to answer the following queries:
a) Display the name and salary of all managers. (2 marks)
b) Display the names, prices and quantities available of items that are not sold. (4 marks)
c) Display the names of employees who had sold both computers and cameras. (5 marks)
d) Display the names of items which has more than 1000 pieces sold. (6 marks)
e) Display the name of the items which are sold the most. (8 marks)

criteria.point: Correctly joins DEPT and EMP to find managers
Uses set difference or outer join to find items not in SALES
Uses intersection or self-join with item name conditions
Uses aggregation (sum) with grouping and having clause
Uses aggregation, ordering, and limiting to find most sold item

questions.model_answer: a) π_eName,salary(DEPT ⨝ EMP). b) π_itemName,price,availableQty(ITEM) - π_itemName,price,availableQty(ITEM ⨝ SALES). c) intersection of employees selling computers and cameras. d) grouping with sum > 1000. e) ordering by sum desc, limit 1.

questions.question_text:
Consider the following relations in a database created for an online store:
Customers(cid, name, phone, country)
Employees(eid, ename, phone, hiredte)
Orders(oid, eid, cid, orderDate, requiredDate, shippedDate)
OrderDetails(oid, productId, quantity, discount)
Products(productId, productName, UnitPrice, unitsInStock, ROL)

a) Use SQL queries to answer the following:
i) Display the name and address of customers who had ordered products which cost over Rs.500. (4 marks)
ii) Find the names and unit prices of all products which has not been ordered by customers from 'Germany'. (5 marks)
iii) Find the customer ids and names of the customers who have obtained more than 5% discount for every product in every order they have placed. (6 marks)
b) Create a view named incomplete_Orders that contains customer name, country and number of times an order is not completed. (7 marks)
c) Create a function named calc_cost to calculate and return the total cost of an order given the order id and the discount. (8 marks)
d) Create a trigger named updateCost to update the cost column when the order details are added to the OrderDetails table. (10 marks)

criteria.point: Correct SQL query with proper JOIN and WHERE clause for products costing over 500
Correct use of NOT IN or EXCEPT to exclude German customers' orders
Correct GROUP BY with HAVING clause checking discount > 5% for ALL orders
Correct CREATE VIEW with JOIN and filtering for incomplete orders
Correct CREATE FUNCTION with proper logic to calculate total cost with discount
Correct CREATE TRIGGER that fires on INSERT and updates cost

questions.model_answer: a) i) SELECT c.name, c.phone FROM Customers c JOIN Orders o ON c.cid=o.cid JOIN OrderDetails od ON o.oid=od.oid JOIN Products p ON od.productId=p.productId WHERE p.UnitPrice > 500; ii) SELECT productName, UnitPrice FROM Products WHERE productId NOT IN (SELECT od.productId FROM OrderDetails od JOIN Orders o ON od.oid=o.oid JOIN Customers c ON o.cid=c.cid WHERE c.country='Germany'); iii) SELECT cid, name FROM Customers WHERE cid NOT IN (SELECT o.cid FROM Orders o JOIN OrderDetails od ON o.oid=od.oid WHERE od.discount <= 0.05); b) CREATE VIEW incomplete_Orders AS SELECT c.name, c.country, COUNT(*) FROM Customers c JOIN Orders o ON c.cid=o.cid JOIN OrderDetails od ON o.oid=od.oid JOIN Products p ON od.productId=p.productId WHERE p.unitsInStock < od.quantity GROUP BY c.name, c.country; c) CREATE FUNCTION calc_cost(@oid INT, @discount REAL) RETURNS REAL AS BEGIN DECLARE @total REAL; SELECT @total = SUM(UnitPrice * quantity * (1-discount)) FROM OrderDetails od JOIN Products p ON od.productId=p.productId WHERE od.oid=@oid; RETURN @total; END; d) CREATE TRIGGER updateCost ON OrderDetails AFTER INSERT AS UPDATE Orders SET cost = (SELECT calc_cost(i.oid, i.discount) FROM inserted i WHERE Orders.oid = i.oid);

guideLines.description: Student must be represented as an entity rectangle.
Student should have Name, Gender, DOB and Age attributes.
Age must be represented as a derived attribute using a dashed ellipse.
College must be represented as an entity rectangle.
College should have Name, Affiliation and Address attributes.
Student and College must be connected through the Enrolls in relationship.
College must be connected to the Specialized in relationship.
Computer Science, Mechanical and Electronics should be represented as entities.
Entities should use rectangles, attributes should use ellipses, relationships should use diamonds, and the derived attribute should use a dashed ellipse.
All entities, attributes and relationships should be connected according to the reference diagram.
